  "screen_decision": "exclude",
  "screen_rationale": "The study uses in vitro cytotoxicity data from human lung epithelial cell lines to predict acute inhalation toxicity in rats. The 'index test' is an in vitro assay (cytotoxicity), not a whole, live non-human animal. Therefore, it does not meet the inclusion criteria.",

  "arm_evidence": "The study investigates the prediction of acute inhalation toxicity, which falls under toxicology.",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "respiratory",

  ],
  "areas_evidence": "The study focuses on acute inhalation toxicity, which is related to the respiratory system. It also has cross-cutting applicability to various substances.",
  "model_type": "across-multiple-models",
  "model_evidence": "The study uses both literature data and experimental data for cytotoxicity assays and compares them to literature LC50 data.",
  "species": [
    "rat"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "The study mentions 'LC50 (rat, inhalation, 4 h)' as a data point.",
  "endpoint_class": "secondary-biomarker",
  "endpoint_evidence": "The study uses IC50 (cytotoxicity) and LC50 (lethal concentration) as endpoints, which are biomarkers of toxicity rather than hard clinical outcomes."
